subject: Music Production
title: The Akai MPC and Its Legacy
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Akai MPC and Its Legacy.

hook.text: Roger Linn designed the MPC60 in 1988, combining a sampler with pressure-sensitive drum pads.

buildup.text: Producers could chop samples and trigger them live by tapping pads, making beatmaking feel physical.

discovery.text: The MPC became the centerpiece of studios for J Dilla, DJ Premier, and Kanye West.

twist.text: J Dilla's loose, off-grid timing on the MPC created a humanized swing that changed modern music.

climax.text: The MPC defined how hip-hop, R&B, and electronic music were made for over two decades.

punchline.text: Tapping rubber pads shaped decades of modern music.

quiz.question: What made the MPC unique compared to earlier samplers?
options: It combined sampling with pressure-sensitive drum pads
